items.title: Canucks Takeaways: Tolopilo’s stellar outing fuels second straight win
items.summary: Nikita Tolopilo had a brilliant 34-save performance on Monday as the Canucks beat the Mammoth for their first winning streak of the season.
items.body: If the plan was to reward third-string goalie Nikita Tolopilo for his fine minor-league play by giving him a National Hockey League start on a back-to-back and then sending him back to the American League, the Vancouver Canucks should rethink things. Of course, we don’t know what the plan is — or was — because NHL teams at the bottom of the standings do not ordinarily clutter their active roster with a third goalie, but Tolopilo’s first game for the Canucks since last season should earn him a longer stay. The 26-year-old goalie, who cleared NHL waivers in September on his way back to the minors, had a brilliant 34-save performance Monday in Salt Lake City as the Canucks beat the Utah Mammoth 3-2 for Vancouver’s first winning streak of the season. After losing 17 of their previous 18 games to pass the quarter mark of their schedule with one of the worst records in NHL history, the Canucks swept the Mammoth and Vegas Golden Knights in just over 24 hours for their first consecutive wins. Stanley Cup contenders, the Knights are a heavy, physical team. The Mammoth are pretty heavy, too, but with considerably more speed and youth. And the Canucks beat them by an aggregate score of 9-5 to re-energize themselves after a bleak, dispiriting start to their rebuild season. Starting goalie Leevi Merilainen was the best Canuck in Vegas, and Tolopilo was even better in Utah. It seemed like a peculiar decision to recall Tolopilo on Sunday to give Merilainen a breather in the back-to-back because Vancouver is stuck with struggling veteran Kevin Lankinen and his no-move-clause contract. items.title: Boeser’s late power-play goal lifts Canucks to win over Mammoth
items.summary: Brock Boeser scored a power-play goal with 4:23 left to lift the Vancouver Canucks to a 3-2 victory over the Utah Mammoth on Monday night.
items.body: SALT LAKE CITY — Brock Boeser scored a power-play goal with 4:23 left to lift the Vancouver Canucks to a 3-2 victory over the Utah Mammoth on Monday night. Jake DeBrusk flicked the puck out to Boeser and he threaded it inside the post to help Vancouver win consecutive games for the first time this season. DeBrusk and Filip Chytil also scored goals for the Canucks. Nikita Tolopilo made 32 saves in his season debut for Vancouver. Vincent Trocheck and Barrett Hayton scored for Utah, which lost is sixth straight game. Karel Vejmelka had 21 stops for the Mammoth. Neither team found the net until DeBrusk chipped in a power-play goal at the post with 4:55 left in the second. Vancouver scored 10 seconds into the power play after Boeser crossed the puck into DeBrusk while he battled Lawson Crouse for position at the post. Trocheck got Utah on the board at 2:51 of the third, snapping in the puck on a power play. The Canucks regained the lead on Chytil’s goal at 4:40 of the third. Chytil drew Vejmelka out to the post, wrapped around the net, and deflected the puck off the goaltender’s heel for the easy goal. Hayton leveled the score again with 8:20 left, snapping the puck over Tolopilo’s shoulder.

items.title: Struggling power play deflates Canadiens in loss to Rangers
items.summary: The sooner the Canadiens can sort out their power play, the better. The unit’s struggles hadn’t been particularly costly up to this point, but an 0-for-4 showing deflated Montreal in Monday’s loss to the Rangers.
items.body: NEW YORK — Any time you give up a goal on your own power play before even registering a shot on net, you know it’s going to be a bad night. It was arguably their worst one since they started their season with a fortunate 3-2 win in Toronto on Sept. 29. That victory over the Maple Leafs was one of two nights in which the Canadiens had all their power-play regulars available to them, which is undeniably part of the reason why their power play has been dysfunctional for the last 19 games. But even without Ivan Demidov—a dynamic, triple-threat player who can shoot, pass and deke opponents to open up all kinds of options—it shouldn’t be this bad. “Demi’s a special player and a threat when he has it, when he’s shooting it,” said Nick Suzuki . “Obviously we miss him, but I feel like we have the talent and the players to make up for that.” Suzuki is one of them, though his six-game absence didn’t help the power play. Cole Caufield , who’s coming off a 51-goal season, has been there all along, and he’s an elite power-play option. As is Juraj Slafkovsky, who scored 15 of his career-high 30 goals last season on the man advantage. And if Lane Hutson isn’t the best power-play quarterback in the league, he isn’t far off. But even with all of them in place and sniper Zachary Bolduc in Demidov’s spot, the Canadiens’ top unit hasn’t clicked. And it takes up too much time for the second unit to pick up the slack. The power play came to New York in an 0-for-10 stretch, and yet Suzuki said a 30-minute video session with coach Martin St. Louis revealed it was, in his words, “definitely not broken.” That was a conclusion based on goals being left on the table—back-door tap-ins unfinished—and if it was an accurate one, it didn’t hold through Monday night at Madison Square Garden. items.title: Canadiens give up three unanswered goals in loss to Rangers
items.body: NEW YORK — Will Cuylle scored twice, including the go-ahead short-handed goal in the final minute of the second period, and the New York Rangers rallied to defeat the Montreal Canadiens 3-1 on Monday night. The Rangers have won three in a row and six of their past seven and improved to 9-2-0 at home. Their latest victory followed a ceremony commemorating the 100th anniversary of the first game in franchise history, which came against the Montreal Maroons. Once the puck dropped, the Canadiens dominated for stretches with the puck in the offensive zone. That allowed them to take the lead when Lane Hutson spun around Matt Rempe and put a shot in the perfect place for Phillip Danault to deflect it into the net. Their advantage lasted less than two minutes. With Juraj Slafkovský slow to guard Marcus Pettersson back down the ice, the defenseman banked the puck off Cuylle in the crease to bring life to a fired-up crowd inside Madison Square Garden. Montreal then showed why it ranks second to last in the NHL on the power play despite overflowing with talent from Hutson and Slafkovský to Cole Caufield and Nick Suzuki. When the top unit failed to score, Alex Newhook missing the net paved the way for Cuylle to get a head of steam and beat Jacob Fowler short side off the rush with 56.3 seconds left in the second. Another unsuccessful Canadiens power play in the third was cut short by an interference penalty on Noah Dobson. Scott Morrow scored just his second career goal with 13:16 left. Fowler allowed three goals on 26 shots. At the other end, Joonas Korpisalo made 24 saves to win for the third time in as many starts since missing the first five-plus weeks of the season because of injury. items.body: Register Login Blues Recall Nathan Walker By Brennan McClain | at November 16, 2026 6:01 pm The St. Louis Blues have added some depth as their forward corps recovers from a few minor injuries. According to a team announcement , the Blues recalled forward Nathan Walker from the Springfield Thunderbirds in the AHL. Walker, 32, earns his first call-up of the 2026-27 season after spending the last two years in the NHL. He’s only two years removed from recording his best NHL season, registering eight goals and 16 points in 73 games, while averaging 12:06 of ice time per game. Shortly before the 2025-26 season, the Blues signed Walker to a two-year, $1.78MM ($887.5K AAV) extension through the 2027-28 season. Moving back into a true depth role last season, Walker finished with four goals and 11 points in 46 games, while averaging 11:59 of ice time. items.body: Blueshirts legend provides fun moment during exhibition to benefit pediatric cancer care New York Rangers legend Henrik Lundqvist scored a goalie goal at the Alumni Classic at Madison Square Garden on Sunday. Late in the annual event with the opposing net empty, Lundqvist gloved a shot by defenseman Brendan Smith , skated out of the crease to his left and let it fly down the ice. 🚨 WE HAVE A HENRIK LUNDQVIST GOAL 🚨 pic.twitter.com/44jBWQvlze Earlier this season before injury ended his season, Rangers goalie Igor Shesterkin scored a goalie goal to the delight of Lundqvist, who was working as an MSG studio analyst for that game. The Maple Leafs finished last season well out of the playoffs, and it was clear that they had a lot of holes in their roster, particularly in their bottom six and on their defense. The team lacked secondary scoring, didn’t have much physicality, needed more speed, and needed to address their goaltender. Maatta, who began his career by quickly earning a pair of Stanley Cup rings with the Pittsburgh Penguins , has become a reliable, experienced journeyman in the second half of his career. The 32-year-old is in his first year in St. Paul after coming over from Calgary as part of the deal that sent Jacob Middleton to the Flames and also brought Blake Coleman to the Wild. The Wild have been one of the hottest teams in the NHL all season long to this point, and their 15-3-4 record is good enough to give them a seven-point lead over the Colorado Avalanche and Nashville Predators , meaning they’ve opened up a sizable lead in what was supposed to be an incredibly competitive division. Minnesota has gone 8-0-2 in its past 10 games, and it will look to keep its lengthy point streak going on Tuesday night when the Predators pay a visit to Grand Casino Arena. "Truth is, I have something in mind," the forward told Czech newspaper Deník Sport in a story published Monday to promote his autobiography, "JA68," and a special line of trading cards. "I'm not sure if people would be interested. But if it were to happen, the ideal date would be around the beginning of August 2027. There will be the World Cup (of Hockey) in Prague during the season after that, but I am not sure I would be able to skate at that time." Several of the 49-year-old’s friends and former teammates participated, including Jagr, Boston Bruins forward David Pastrnak , and fellow Hockey Hall of Famers Ray Bourque , Mark Recchi , Marian Hossa and Patrice Bergeron . "I would like to bring in some really high-quality players," Jagr said. "Former teammates, but also players who are still active, to make sure the game is played at a high level. If you have nothing more to give and you feel like you’re doing more harm than good, it’s time to leave. But I think I’ve squeezed every last drop out of it.” Jagr last played in the NHL nine years ago, putting an end to one of the greatest careers in NHL history. Since then, he has played for Rytíři Kladno, the Czech Extraliga club that Jagr is a part owner of. items.body: CALGARY — Five games into the season, it appeared Flames fans, and their franchise, were finally going to experience the pain of what a true rebuild looks and feels like. Allowing an astounding 27 goals, the young squad only scored eight times as part of a boys-vs.-men optic the locals figured they might have to get used to as part of the organization’s first full-fledged reconstruction. Even Landon DuPont likely started wondering if he should start looking for a Beltline condo, assuming he would be selected first overall by his hometown Flames in next summer’s draft. But what followed was an impressive show of resilience, spurred on by tremendous coaching, leadership and character in a room full of hungry youngsters who turned the season on a dime. They won five of their next six, seven of their next 10 and now hit the quarter mark with a 9-11-1 record, just a few wins back of the playoff spot they are likely still several years away from. items.title: Leafs GM Chayka gives coach Jim Hiller vote of confidence
items.summary: The Maple Leafs have had a miserable start to the 2026-27 season, but it seems to be in favor of keep their head coach on board.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Amid a terrible two months to start the 2026-27 season, the Toronto Maple Leafs ‘ brass seems to be sticking with the process. When speaking to the media on Monday, Maple Leafs general manager John Chayka publicly gave a vote of confidence to head coach Jim Hiller. “We got a lot of confidence in Jim,” Chayka said. “Mats and I have our full support behind him. And I think adversity is an opportunity to learn, an opportunity to grow. I think you have really have to be honest where you’re at, what you’ve done, what needs to improve.” It has been a rocky start to the Jim Hiller era in Toronto. The man who Chayka hired has done little to help the team improve after missing out on the Stanley Cup Playoffs last season. As of Monday, the team is on a six-game losing streak, losing eight of their past nine. Toronto lost each matchup in its recent four-game homestand, capped off with a 1-0 loss to the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday night. The consistent failure of the Leafs through the first quarter of the new season is having fans call for an immediate change behind the bench. When chatting with reporters, Chayka added that “fans deserve better,” something he said a couple of times. Yet, no changes seem to be coming from the Original Six franchise at this time. Toronto currently ranks 27th in the NHL in goals allowed (76) and just 12th in goals scored (69), which is far from promising given the offensive weapons they have in the lineup. The Leafs (8-12-2) are last in the Atlantic Division, nine points back of a Wild Card spot in the Eastern Conference. They will look to get back in the win column on Tuesday night, when they visit the struggling Chicago Blackhawks .

items.title: Sweden beat Finland in shootout to win 2026 Women’s Worlds bronze medal
items.summary: Sweden knocked off their rivals to win their first medal in a major international tournament since 2007.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images The drought is over. Thanks to Ebba Svensson Traff’s heroics in the shootout, Sweden defeated Finland to win the bronze medal at the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship. It is Sweden’s first medal at the Women’s Worlds since 2007, and the program’s third bronze medal overall. Finland came short of winning a record 16th bronze at the WWC. In another thrilling battle between the Scandinavian rivals. Back and forth, the two teams traded chances, but neither could find the back of the net until Michelle Karvinen tipped in an Elisa Holopainen point shot on the power play for her second of the tournament, putting the Finns out in front. Sweden managed to use the player advantage to level the game in the waning minutes of regulation, as Lina Ljungblom finished off a nice feed from Hanna Thuvik for her second of the tournament. After neither team scored for the remainder of regulation, overtime was required. However, both Svensson Traff and Sanni Ahola made some big saves in the extra frame. In the skills competition, Tilde Grillfors and Hilda Svensson both scored for the Swedes, while Noora Tulus was the only one to find the back of the net for Finland, through Karvinen rang one off the crossbar. Sweden outshot Finland 37-30 in the contest. Along with her three saves in the shootout, Svensson Traff turned away 29 shots in the victorious effort. Ahola made 35 stops in the loss. It was a little bit of redemption for Sweden, a team that lost to Switzerland in an exciting bronze medal clash at the 2026 Winter Olympics. items.summary: The Sharks have won their past two games as their dynamic duo of Smith and Celebrini has combined for eight points.

But with just two consecutive wins, the Sharks have bounced back to fourth in the Pacific Division and now sit just one point back of the Utah Mammoth for the Western Conference’s second wild card spot. Those two wins, by margins of 6-5 in a shootout over the Mammoth and 4-2 over the surprisingly strong Nashville Predators , have been powered by major offensive production from star forwards Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith, who combined for eight points across the two victories. Celebrini had been held pointless in 5 of the 11 games prior to this mini-streak, while Smith had just four points in the first six games of November. Fitzgerald joins the Panthers’ organization fresh off a six-year stint as the general manager of the New Jersey Devils that ended when he was dismissed following a disappointing 2025-26 season for the Devils. Fitzgerald first joined the Devils’ front office as an assistant GM in 2015, and he took over the head job in January of 2020 after the late Ray Shero was let go. The Massachusetts native was the 17th overall pick in the 1986 NHL Draft and had a 17-year playing career at the NHL level with the New York Islanders , Panthers, Colorado Avalanche , Nashville Predators , Chicago Blackhawks , Toronto Maple Leafs and Boston Bruins . Fitzgerald appeared in 1,097 career regular season games, posting 329 points on 139 goals and 190 assists. Under Fitzgerald’s watch, the Devils qualified for the Stanley Cup Playoffs twice. In 2023, they ousted their archrival New York Rangers before falling to the Carolina Hurricanes in the second round, and they met a similar fate in 2025 when the Hurricanes knocked them out in five games in the first round. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Brett Holmes-Imagn Images A rising star in the game has put himself in some rare air. On Sunday night, Anaheim Ducks forward Cutter Gauthier scored his 14th goal in the month of November, helping the Ducks come away with a 6-1 win over the Calgary Flames. The goal not only highlighted what has been an incredible run for Gauthier, but he became just the third player in the last century of the NHL to score 14 or more goals in a single month, joining Hockey Hall of Famers Wayne Gretzky and Mario Lemieux. With that goal, Gauthier also extended his goal streak to nine games , the NHL’s longest run in 29 years. The last time a player found the back of the net that many times in a row was legend Teemu Selanne, who scored in 11 straight games with the Mighty Ducks from October to November 1997. It has been a thrilling past couple of weeks for the former Boston College standout. He posted back-to-back hat tricks to start November, scoring three goals for a third time on Nov. 8 against the Pittsburgh Penguins , becoming the first NHLer to post three hat tricks in a 10-day span to begin a month. Thanks to his incredible performance so far in November, the 22-year-old is now just six goals away from matching the NHL record for goals in a single month (20), set by Selanne in March 1993 and Joe Malone in February 1921. Gauthier has seven games to reach that mark. Gauthier is also riding an 11-game point streak, a little bit behind the current point-streak leader in the clubhouse, Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid (22 games). items.body: WINNIPEG — The Winnipeg Jets have hit the quarter-mark of the 2026-27 NHL season still trying to figure out who they are. Through 21 games, the Jets are 10-8-3, sitting sixth in the Central Division and tied with the Utah Mammoth for the final wild-card playoff spot in the Western Conference. Is Winnipeg closer to the club that was once mired in a nine-game losing streak? Or are the Jets more like the team that has now ripped off six straight victories, twice erasing a four-goal deficit? While a playoff berth felt like a pipe dream earlier in the season, the recent turnaround has made the Jets must-watch TV. There are still some major questions about this franchise, and nailing down consistency will be key. But you need to find a rhythm before you round into form, and the Jets have certainly found theirs. This might sound like a troll job. After all, Winnipeg is still led by its stars. Both Mark Scheifele and Kyle Connor are collecting points at a historic pace, with Scheifele's four-point night in Saturday's win over Chicago putting him ahead of mentor Dale Hawerchuk for most points in club history. Connor's 17 goals in 21 games have him on pace to crush his career-high of 47 set in the 2021-22 campaign. items.summary: Martin St. Louis was steadfast in his belief that the Canadiens should embrace their contender status, not waste time debating it. So far there hasn’t been much of a debate, Eric Engels writes in his quarter-mark report card.
items.body: NEW YORK — When we sat down with Montreal Canadiens coach Martin St. Louis before the season got underway, he talked about how his team should embrace its contender status and waste no time debating whether it’s been earned. “I think the biggest thing for our group to understand is this is where we are,” St. Louis said. “We won two playoff rounds; let’s accept this is where we are. We have to understand how we got here, because it wasn’t luck. Luck has nothing to do with why we’re here. Are we on time? Are we ahead? Who cares, this is where we are. When you accept where you are, now there’s more responsibilities. We had to accept where we were two years ago and get to work. Now that we’ve gotten to where we are today, we have to accept it and embrace the bigger responsibilities that come with it to move forward.” After the Canadiens completed their 20th game Saturday — a hard-fought loss that ended a 9-0-3 streak — who would debate that they haven't done exactly that? With one of their best and most complete performances in what has been a historically bad season so far, the Canucks got goals from throughout their lineup, a 34-save performance from goalie Leevi Merilainen and timely responses whenever the Golden Knights pressed them. It was proof of what Vancouver coach Manny Malhotra has been preaching: that when the Canucks play a simple, direct game and play it for three periods, the National Hockey League’s last-place team can be competitive. The win ended a seven-game losing streak in which the Canucks didn’t once make it to overtime, and was just Vancouver’s second victory of any kind since Oct. 3. They had lost an unfathomable 17 out of 18 games, starting with a 3-2 home loss against Vegas on Oct. 4. The Canucks played well for stretches in many of those games, but had been unable to maintain effort and execution through three periods. Nearly all of their losses have featured periods in which the Canucks lost their discipline tactically or simply disappeared competitively. On Sunday, they didn’t allow a poor shift or a goal against to torpedo them or send the team reeling for 10 or 15 minutes. And importantly, when the Knights did press them and drew within one goal, the Canucks quickly answered back with goals from Filip Chytil and Drew O’Connor. items.body: LAS VEGAS — Filip Chytil and Linus Karlsson each scored twice and the Vancouver Canucks snapped a seven-game losing streak with a 6-3 victory over the Vegas Golden Knights on Sunday night. Elias Pettersson and Drew O’Connor also scored for the Canucks. Leevi Merilainen stopped 34 shots. Brock Boeser had two assists to extend his points streak to seven games. Victor Olofsson, Braeden Bowman and Mark Stone scored for the Golden Knights. Carter Hart, who made 21 saves, allowed three or more goals for the fifth time this season. Vancouver ended an eight-game losing streak against Vegas and halted the Golden Knights’ six-game points streak. The Canucks had lost nine of their previous 10 games. Stone’s power-play goal at 1:24 of the third period cut the deficit to 4-3 and gave him 417 points with the Golden Knights, tying Jonathan Marchessault’s franchise record. O’Connor answered just 24 seconds later to restore Vancouver’s two-goal cushion. Karlsson added an empty-net goal with 2:14 remaining. Chytil, activated from injured reserve Friday, scored his first two goals of the season. He tipped in a shot with 2:24 left in the first period for a 3-1 lead, then scored short0handed at 2:14 of the second to make it 4-1. Pettersson opened the scoring on a power play at 5:20 of the first, and Karlsson doubled the lead at 9:49. Olofsson’s power-play goal at 13:30 extended his goals streak to three games. Bowman cut Vancouver’s lead to 4-2 with 8:03 to go in the second. Mitch Marner had two assists for Vegas, extending his home points streak to 11 games. Today, we look at the race for the Calder Trophy , given annually to the best rookie in the NHL as selected in a poll by the Professional Hockey Writers Association. Montreal Canadiens goalie Jacob Fowler has emerged as the early favorite for the Calder Trophy less than a month after beginning the season in the American Hockey League. Fowler received 68 voting points, including 12 of 15 for first place, to finish first in a poll of NHL.com writers for the trophy awarded annually to the NHL rookie of the year. items.title: Jason Robertson scores overtime goal to lift Stars past Panthers
items.body: DALLAS — Jason Robertson scored at 2:56 of overtime to lift the Dallas Stars past the Florida Panthers 2-1 on Sunday night. Robertson took a pass from Roope Hintz and scored on a backhander for his team-leading 10th goal this season and his seventh career overtime score. Dallas’ Casey DeSmith won the matchup of backup goaltenders with 25 saves while Florida’s Akira Schmid stopped 20 shots. Wyatt Johnston also scored for the Stars, who snapped a six-game losing streak against the Panthers, beating them for the first time since Jan. 8, 2023. Matthew Tkachuk scored for the Panthers, who had a three-game winning streak snapped. Both teams completed a back-to-back and played a third game in four nights. Dallas won both, shutting out Buffalo 2-0 on Saturday and completing a 3-1-0 homestand. Florida won 4-1 at St. Louis on Saturday. Tkachuk opened the scoring with a power-play goal at 4:27 of the second period with a shot from the right circle off the bottom of the crossbar, with brother Brady screening DeSmith, for his 700th career NHL point. It was only the fourth goal allowed by Dallas’ league-best home penalty kill in 45 shorthanded situations. Johnston tied the score about five minutes later when he controlled a cross-ice pass from Thomas Harley and scored easily with Schmid on the far side of the net. Three of Florida’s skaters had been on the ice for close to two minutes. items.summary: Leon Draisaitl scored twice and Connor McDavid had a goal and two assists, in the process tying a 42-year-old NHL milestone set by Wayne Gretzky, as the Edmonton Oilers beat the Philadelphia Flyers 5-2 on Sunday night.
items.body: PHILADELPHIA — Leon Draisaitl scored twice and Connor McDavid had a goal and two assists, in the process tying a 42-year-old NHL milestone set by Wayne Gretzky, as the Edmonton Oilers beat the Philadelphia Flyers 5-2 on Sunday night. McDavid wasted little time getting his 40th assist of the season, his slick backhand pass setting up Draisaitl for a power-play goal 8:08 into the game. McDavid tied former Oilers star Gretzky’s 1984-85 NHL mark of fastest player to 40 assists in a season, with both doing so in their 22nd games. The Oilers have now won five straight and lead the NHL with 35 points. McDavid, leads the NHL with 53 points (12 goals, 41 assists) and Draisaitl is the first to reach 20 goals this season. Vasily Podkolzin and Zach Hyman also scored for Edmonton ands Evan Bouchard had a pair of assists. Tristan Jarry made 34 saves. Cole Knuble and Noah Cates scored second-period goals for the Flyers, who were 0 for 8 on the power play. McDavid was active on another Edmonton power play in the opening period, shoveling a puck to Podkolzin who shot into a crowd. He was credited with an unassisted goal when a Philadelphia player inadvertently knocked the puck past goaltender Dan Vladar at 13:22. Just more than five minutes later, McDavid passed to Hyman, who curled a shot past Vladar’s glove to make it 3-0. Vladar had 16 saves. Knuble cut the lead to 3-1 in the second before Cates slipped alone into the slot and scored on a pass from Matvei Michkov at 17:12 to make it 3-2. Moments after a Flyers power play expired in the opening minute of the third period, however, Draisaitl picked off Travis Konecny's pass, broke in alone and scored for a 4-2 lead. McDavid scored his 12th goal of the season into an empty net with 1:08 left.

items.summary: With two assists on Sunday, McDavid has 41 assists through 22 games this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Connor McDavid has been making hockey look far too easy so far in the 2026-27 NHL season, and the Edmonton Oilers star center just earned yet another eye-popping accomplishment. During the Oilers’ 5-2 win over the Philadelphia Flyers on Sunday, McDavid notched a goal and two assists, giving him 41 assists through 22 games played this season. That ties Wayne Gretzky’s mark from the 1984-85 season for the fewest games to reach 40 assists to start a season. McDavid, 29, had already become the fastest player in NHL history to reach 30 assists this season, when he had an assist in a 4-1 win over the New York Rangers on November 1 to accomplish the feat in 15 games. By getting on the score sheet on Sunday, McDavid also extended his career-best point streak to 22 games. The Oilers’ captain has always been a dominant offensive force, but he’s been scoring at an especially ridiculous rate this season. With his three points against the Flyers, McDavid has 12 goals and 41 assists for 53 points in 22 games. That puts him on pace for a 200-point season, which is something that has only ever been achieved by Gretzky, who did so four times for Edmonton in the 1980s. Even if McDavid cools off a bit from his current torrid pace, he still stands a very strong chance to have the best scoring season of his career. His most productive season to date came in 2022-23, when he registered 64 goals and 89 assists for 153 points in all 82 games. The three-time Hart Trophy winner has led Edmonton to 35 points through 22 games, good for first place in the Pacific Division . The Oilers will continue their current six-game road trip when they visit the Florida Panthers on Tuesday.

items.body: Connor McDavid is showing shades of Wayne Gretzky once again. The Edmonton Oilers captain tied Gretzky's record for the fewest games to record 40 assists, doing so in his 22nd contest of the season against the Philadelphia Flyers on Sunday. McDavid took a pass from Leon Draisaitl in the slot and fed a backhand pass right back to his linemate for a one-timer power-play goal. It came one day after McDavid extended his point streak to a career-best 21 games and reached 50 points on the season with an assist to Evan Bouchard against the Maple Leafs on Saturday. However, the 29-year-old superstar is still far from that record. Gretzky holds the NHL record for the longest point streak at 51 games, which he set in the 1983-84 season with the Oilers. Gretzky piled up a ridiculous 61 goals and 92 assists over the 51-game streak, and went on to finish the season with 205 points. McDavid, now at 11 goals and 41 assists over his 22-game tear, is on pace for 199 points this season. Only Gretzky has ever surpassed the 200-point mark, a feat he accomplished four times over his career.

items.body: Register Login Rangers Move Igor Shesterkin To Season-Ending LTIR By Brian La Rose | at November 15, 2026 5:00 pm The Rangers have quietly made a move to open up considerably more salary cap flexibility. PuckPedia reports ( Twitter link ) that the Rangers have transferred goaltender Igor Shesterkin from regular LTIR to season-ending LTIR. The placement means that the netminder won’t be able to return at any point in 2026-27, either in the regular season or the playoffs. Considering he was ruled out for the season when he sustained a leg injury last month, the Rangers aren’t really taking any sort of risk making this move. When a player goes on regular LTIR, the cap flexibility created is capped at the lower of the player’s AAV or last year’s average salary, roughly $3.9MM this season. That amount is also reduced by the amount of regular cap space the team has at the time. This is the route New York initially took, giving them ample flexibility to recall Dylan Garand at the time of the injury and make other needed roster moves as well. However, when a player is moved to season-ending LTIR, the player’s full cap hit becomes spendable again, minus any existing cap room or existing LTIR usage. That’s especially notable when you consider that Shesterkin has the highest cap hit for a goalie in NHL history, checking in at $11,567,857. Per PuckPedia , the Rangers now have roughly $9MM in LTIR room at their disposal after today’s acquisition of Arvid Soderblom . They technically didn’t need to make this move to facilitate the trade as they had nearly $3MM in regular LTIR room beforehand and Soderblom only cut down about half of that. items.body: Former NHL forward talks going undrafted, finding identity, transitioning to current job Welcome to the NHL Chat Room, NHL.com's Q&A feature where we talk to key figures in the game, gaining insight into their lives on and off the ice. This week, we feature Karl Stewart, who was named vice president and director of NHL Central Scouting in July after seven seasons as an amateur scout with the Washington Capitals. Karl Stewart can trace his path to becoming director of NHL Central Scouting through the people who helped him see what was possible. Colin Campbell and Mike Murphy provided his first scouting job with NHL Central Scouting when his playing career ended, and Ross Mahoney showed him with the Washington Capitals how character should matter when evaluating players and building a staff. items.title: MacKinnon out one month, Makar two weeks for Avalanche
items.summary: Nathan MacKinnon will be out one month, and Cale Makar will be sidelined two weeks, Colorado Avalanche coach Jared Bednar announced before their 4-1 win against the Montreal Canadiens on Saturday.
items.body: Nathan MacKinnon will be out one month, and Cale Makar will be sidelined two weeks, Colorado Avalanche coach Jared Bednar announced before their 4-1 win against the Montreal Canadiens on Saturday. Each sustained a lower-body injury in the second period of a 4-3 overtime loss to the Ottawa Senators on Thursday. MacKinnon's last shift came with 8:15 remaining in the second. The center grabbed his right side after attempting a reverse hit on Senators defenseman Artem Zub and stayed on the bench for a few minutes before heading down the tunnel. Makar took a shift at 10:44 of the second that lasted only four seconds before heading to the locker room. The defenseman briefly returned for a 23-second shift that ended with 5:20 remaining, but stayed on the bench for the rest of the period. The injury came four days after he left practice on Nov. 8 for precautionary reasons. "When I think about those two guys, it's like every matchup, they take it on, now someone else has to be able to step up and do that," Bednar said. "And then you are losing the depth down the lineup as you kind of do that because everyone is elevated." MacKinnon leads Colorado and is tied for fifth in the NHL with 30 points (10 goals, 20 assists) in 20 games; Makar is third on the Avalanche and tied for third among NHL defensemen with 23 points (five goals, 18 assists) in 19 games. "Probably the most important is the 5-on-5 offense that they create," Bednar said. "We can be playing an OK game, chances equal, tight game, and those guys, like the top players do, will find a way to make a play that's a difference-maker for you. Whether it's Cale or 'Mac,' or both of them combined, they generally win us a lot of hockey games because of that. So with out that, the rest of the game has to tighten up and get better.

In a corresponding roster move, radio host Brendan Batchelor reported that the Canucks have recalled netminder Nikita Tolopilo . Quillan, 24, began the year with the Toronto Maple Leafs organization, playing for the Toronto Marlies. After nearly averaging a point per game with the Marlies last season, Quillan failed to register any points in his first four games this year. On October 15th, the Maple Leafs traded Quillan to the Canucks in the Aatu Räty deal. The former collegiate free agent got off to a great start with Abbotsford, scoring five goals and seven points in five games. That performance motivated Vancouver to recall Quillan when Filip Chytil landed on the injured reserve. In three games with the Canucks, Quillan registered an assist and 12 PIMs. Meanwhile, the Canucks are looking for another option between the pipes. items.title: Bill Watters, longtime NHL executive and broadcaster, dead at 83
items.body: Bill Watters, an NHL executive, player agent and Sportsnet broadcaster, has passed away. He was 83. Though Watters, of Orillia, Ont., became known for his work in hockey, he began his sports career as a football player, starring for the University of Toronto as a linebacker. He was then selected second overall by the Toronto Argonauts in the 1964 CFL draft, but never played a game after a knee injury in training camp. Watters went on to work with Hockey Canada as an assistant manager for the 1977 and 1978 world championships before joining the Toronto Maple Leafs as an assistant GM for 12 years beginning in 1991. "A longtime member of the team's front office, Bill was an important part of my time as a player with the Maple Leafs and someone I will remember with affection," Maple Leafs senior executive advisor of hockey operations Mats Sundin said Sunday. "Bill cared deeply about the Leafs, the City of Toronto, and the people around him. "On behalf of the Maple Leafs organization, I would like to express our sincere condolences to Bill's family, friends and everyone who had the privilege of knowing him. He will be missed." After his Leafs tenure ended, Watters turned to broadcasting, co-hosting Sportsnet's Hockey Central and Prime Time Sports on 590 The Fan upon its 1989 debut. Watters was also a player agent, representing Maple Leafs such as Rick Vaive.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Danny Wild-Imagn Images The New York Rangers made a quiet but notable transaction on Sunday, as they have moved goaltender Igor Shesterkin from long-term injured reserve to season-ending injured reserve.
